question_text: In this verse, does the characteristic operate in the person's movement toward God — seeking, supplication, worship, covenant — and if so how? Record none if it does not.

distinct_answers.text: Two directions. (1) Human hatred of God (group 3596 — 14 verses): "those who hate me" (Exo 20:5) — hating God is the defining inner orientation of those in covenant rupture. (2) Human hatred of evil as covenant alignment (group 550-NEW-02): Psa 97:10: "O you who love the Lord, hate evil!" — hating what God hates is an act of covenant participation. These are opposite expressions of the same relational orientation toward God.

The dominant movement is the human's contempt directed toward God: despising his name (Mal 1:6), treating his table as despicable (Mal 1:7, 12), spurning his counsel (Psa 107:11), saying in the heart "you will not call to account" (Psa 10:13). The inner posture required to sustain this is covenantal presumption — the assumption that God's claims are negotiable. Contempt toward God operates from within the covenantal relationship, making it a form of covenant betrayal from within.

The righteous abhorrence of evil as covenant alignment: Psa 119:163: "I hate and abhor falsehood, but I love your law" — the abhorrence of falsehood is the negative expression of what loving God's law means positively. In the inverted form: abhorring justice (Amo 5:10, Mic 3:9) is the inner movement away from God — those who abhor what God loves are moving against him in their inner constitution.

The ruthlessness of M06-D is the inner condition of those who have most comprehensively moved away from God — "they do not set God before themselves" (Psa 54:3). The ruthless person's inner movement is the maximum possible distance from God in the M06 cluster — not merely despising him or hating him but removing him from the inner governing framework entirely.

The dominant human-to-God movement in M06-E is appeal. Joel 2:17: "spare your people, O Lord, and make not your heritage a reproach." Psa 119:39: "turn away the reproach that I dread." Lam 5:1: "remember, O Lord, what has befallen us; look, and see our disgrace." The characteristic does not generate human contempt or hatred toward God — it generates the opposite: intense appeal from within the condition of being reproached.

Appeal is the dominant human-to-God movement. Psa 35:1: "contend, O Lord, with those who contend with me." Jer 18:19: "hear me, O Lord, and listen to the voice of my adversaries." The person facing an adversary turns to God and asks him to contend. The human-to-God movement in M06-F is the appeal-posture in the context of adversarial opposition.
No verse in M06-G shows malice operating in the human person's movement toward God. The malice of the nations is directed at Israel; God is named only as the judge of that malice. Silent.

Yes — the great commandment (Mat 22:37 — Group 1542) is primarily a human-toward-God direction: "you shall love the Lord your God." The entire love-toward-God register is the human-to-God direction of M05-A.

Absent as a giving direction — humans never show compassion toward God in the verse evidence. The human-to-God direction for compassion is petitionary only: appealing to God's compassion, not showing it toward him. This is a structural asymmetry: compassion flows only downward (from greater to lesser), and the human is never the greater in relation to God.

Absent — the mercy cry (Group 1629) is human petitioning God's mercy, not showing mercy toward God. The directional asymmetry of mercy (flows from authority toward helplessness) structurally prevents the human-to-God direction.

Partial and limited — the evidence in M05-D does not focus on goodness or kindness as a mode of the person's inner movement toward God. The characteristic primarily operates horizontally toward others.

Yes — a.na.vah/an.vah (Groups 1272, 1271) is constitutively oriented toward God: "humility and fear of the Lord" (Pro 22:4 — Group 1272); "seek humility" before God (Zep 2:3 — Group 1272). The Hebrew humility-meekness vocabulary is primarily the creature's appropriate vertical orientation before God.

Partial — the seeking of comfort from God (Psa 119:82 — Group 1741: "when will you comfort me?") is the human-to-God direction in the seeking/petitionary sense. Human comfort-giving toward God is structurally impossible (same asymmetry as compassion and mercy).

Yes — walking in the light as the condition for fellowship with God (1Jo 1:7 — Group 1055); sharing in Christ's sufferings (Phili 3:10 — Group 1055). The human actively participates in the vertical fellowship through moral orientation and willing suffering-sharing.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — the appeal to God's righteousness as the ground of petition is the primary human-to-God movement in A1. "In your righteousness deliver me" (Psa 31:1; 71:2; 143:1; 143:11, VSG M26-A1-004). The psalmist moves toward God through his righteousness — it becomes the ground of approach, of petition, of confident appeal. God's righteousness is not an obstacle to approach but the most secure ground of it.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — "everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him" (1Jo 2:29, VSG M26-A2-014) — practicing righteousness is itself an orientation toward God: it is the expression of the new birth. Walking with God (M26-A2-014) is the relational mode of human righteousness — righteousness as the orientation of the person toward God. Bringing offerings "in righteousness" (Mal 3:3, VSG M26-A2-014) — worship as the righteous person's movement toward God.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — "whoever walks in uprightness fears the Lord" (Pro 14:2, VSG 1211-002). The walk in uprightness is simultaneously a walk toward the Lord — the two are inseparable. The preparation before God in prayer (a.rakh, Psa 5:3, VSG 6753-003 in the F-group): preparing oneself before God as an act of devotional orientation — the reckoning faculty in its devotional mode.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — receiving justification by faith is itself a movement toward God: the person who believes God (Rom 4:3–5) is turning toward him, accepting the basis he has provided for right standing. Justification creates the conditions for ongoing approach to God through the new standing it establishes.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the cry for justice (Luk 18:3; Rev 6:10, VSG 944-001) is the primary human-to-God movement in D. The wronged person turns to God rather than to themselves — this is an act of faith and dependence: bringing the injustice to God and trusting him to respond.
**[E — Condemnation]** Freedom from condemnation enables movement toward God — but E itself does not primarily describe a human-to-God movement. Silence on direct human-to-God direction in E.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — "count yourselves dead to sin and alive to God" (Rom 6:11) — the reckoning toward God is a movement of orientation: the person reckons themselves as belonging to and alive for God. The devotional preparation (a.rakh, Psa 5:3, VSG 6753-003): preparing oneself before God in prayer is the reckoning faculty directed toward God in worship.

**[CLUSTER — T4.2]** E. The human-to-God interface is present across the cluster: appeal on the basis of divine righteousness (A1), righteous living as movement toward God (A2), upright walk toward the Lord (B), receiving justification by faith (C), the cry for justice as dependent prayer (D), and the reckoning of oneself as alive to God (F). The cluster reveals that righteousness in all its modes orients the person toward God — it is constitutively God-ward.

VCG02 (1Cor 11:31 in M15-D, but proximate): self-discernment directed toward God. VCG01 (sa.khal corpus): attending to God's acts.
VCG04 (Hos 6:3): "let us press on to know the LORD" — human pursuit of knowing God. VCG08: Job's assertions of knowing his Redeemer — addressed toward God.
VCG02 (1Cor 11:31): self-discernment before God. VCG01 (sa.khal corpus): attending to God's revealed acts and ways.
VCG05 (Pro 16:9): human planning submitted to God's governance. VCG07 inverse (Exo 7:23): Pharaoh's refusal to attend — the blocking of human-to-God movement.
VCG03 (Psa 119:97): meditation on God's law as a relational act directed toward God in love.
VCG03 (2Chr 1:10): Solomon's prayer-request directed toward God. VCG01 (2Cor 10:5b): taking thoughts captive to obey Christ.
VCG02 (Col 4:6 corpus): gracious human speech in response to God's word offered in God's service. VCG03 (Gal 5:14): fulfilling the logos of the law as human-to-God movement.

Yes — Phili 4:6: "by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God" — the command against anxiety is paired with prayer-movement toward God. The person's response to anxiety is to turn toward God in prayer. 1Pe 5:7 — the act of casting anxieties onto God is itself a movement toward God.

2Cor 1:8-9 — Paul's response to despair is the theological recognition that this makes the person rely on God who raises the dead — the movement from despair toward God is mediated by theological reframing, not immediate experiential resolution.

Luk 18:1 — the parable of the widow and the judge grounds not-losing-heart in persistent prayer toward God. The movement toward God in prayer is specifically the alternative to ekkakeō — prayer and not-losing-heart are the same inner movement.
Jam 4:8 — "draw near to God and he will draw near to you; cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded" — the remedy for dipsuchos is explicitly a movement toward God.

Yes — extensively in two modes: (1) Supplication: the entire cha.nan corpus (984-001, 72 verses) is the human cry for grace directed upward to God — "be gracious to me, O Lord" (Psa 4:1; 6:2; 27:7; 51:1; etc.). This is the human moving toward God specifically in the grace-seeking posture. (2) Worship-blessing: ba.rakh group 1299-002 — the human blessing of God in worship (Psa 34:1; 103:1; 16:7). The blessing-directed-upward is the doxological response: the creature acknowledging God's worth through the grace-vocabulary directed upward.

DŌRON SUPPLEMENTARY (Phase 10, 2026-05-14):

Luk 21:4 (6837-006): "she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on." The widow's total self-offering from inner trust is the most complete human-to-God giving-act in the dōron corpus — complete inner surrender expressed through complete material offering. Mat 2:11 (6837-001): the Magi's gifts as an act of inner worship and prostration before the child. Both verses evidence the human-to-God direction of grace enacted through material gift.

Partial. The volitional-surrender register (tov group 542-001 — 2Sa 15:26: "let him do to me what seems good to him") shows the human surrendering their will to divine disposition — an act of movement toward God in trust. Pro 15:2 (632-002) — the wise tongue commending knowledge — approaches this through wisdom rather than direct God-directed movement.

M46-C evidences the most direct human-to-God movement in the wealth domain: Pro 3:9 ("honour the Lord with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce") — the material goods are directed toward God in an act of worship. Isa 33:6 (the fear of the Lord is Zion's treasure) — the human movement toward the fear of God is named as the path to the true cho.sen.

M46-D's poverty of spirit (Mat 5:3) is the fundamental human posture toward God: the condition of having nothing to offer, standing open and receptive before God. The learned contentment of Phil 4:11-13 is framed as a posture toward God — "I can do all things through him who strengthens me" (Phil 4:13) — the contentment rests in relationship with God.

The human-to-God movement is precisely what inner closure blocks: the person who trusts in their wealth does not trust in God (Psa 52:7). The sha.a.nan (complacent ease) produces the failure to seek God. The M46-A movement is the absence of or resistance to the human-to-God direction.

M01-A extensively documents the human person moving toward God in reverential fear: (1) **worship** — Psa 5:7 (fear drawing the psalmist into the temple — "reverence for who God is motivates his approach to the temple and shapes his posture of bowing down"); Heb 12:28 (fear and awe as "the fitting inner disposition for approaching God in worship"); (2) **prayer** — Dan 9:4 (reverential fear of God as the inner disposition from which Daniel's prayer arises); Jer 26:19 (Hezekiah's fear producing active prayer that averted disaster); (3) **covenant** — Mal 2:5 (Levi's reverential fear as the covenant response to God's gift of life and peace — fear governing the covenant relationship); (4) **vow** — Jon 1:16 (the sailors' fear leading to sacrifice and vows — fear becoming the ground of devotion).

M01-E-VCG-02 shows the human person trembling before God's word as a specific mode of movement toward God: Isa 66:2 (trembling at God's word as the inner posture God looks for — the human person responsive before divine communication); Ezr 9:4; 10:3 (those who tremble at God's commandment gathering for covenant decision-making — trembling as the posture of covenant engagement).

M01-B shows movement toward God through the theophanic fear and subsequent worship: Jon 1:16 (storm-terror converting to reverential worship — "fear becomes the inner ground of devotion"); Mat 27:54 (centurion's fear producing confession — "Truly this was the Son of God"); Mat 9:8 (crowd's fear "moves inward immediately into glorifying God" — fear as gateway to worship).

The human-to-God movement across M01 is most extensively documented in M01-A (worship, prayer, covenant, vow) and M01-E-VCG-02 (trembling-at-word as the posture of receptive covenant engagement). M01-B shows fear functioning as a gateway to worship when the fear is triggered by encounter with divine power.

Yes. Act 17:16 (M02-D-VCG-03): Paul's spirit provoked by idolatry shows moral-anger as the inner state that drives toward God in righteous concern — the provocation orients him toward God's honor. M02-E-VCG-03: Elijah (1Ki 19:10; 19:14) and the psalmist (Psa 69:9; 119:139) show jealous zeal for God's honor as the inner state of the person who moves toward God in devoted service. The characteristic in its jealous-zeal register is a movement-toward-God characteristic.

Gen 18:30 and 18:32 (M02-B-VCG-05): Abraham's intercession is structured around managing and not triggering God's anger — the human person's movement toward God in petition is shaped by the real threat of God's anger. The prayer is a movement toward God precisely because the anger is real.

This is the most extensively evidenced relational direction in the entire cluster. M03-D-VCG-01 (56 verses) is almost entirely constituted by distress operating in the human person's movement toward God: "call upon me in the day of trouble" (Psa 50:15); "in my distress I cried to the Lord" (Psa 18:6 — anchor); God answers and delivers from all distress. M03-A-VCG-02 (36 verses) is the penitential weeping VCG — tears directed toward God as petition, intercession, and confession. M03-E-VCG-01 names groaning as the inner cry rising to God: Israel's groan under slavery rises to God (Exo 2:24 — anchor).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes — this is the dominant direction in the corpus. The vast majority of VCG-01's 58 verses show human exultation directed toward God: "my soul will rejoice in the Lord" (Psa 35:9); "I will greatly rejoice in the Lord; my soul shall exult in my God" (Isa 61:10); "yet I will rejoice in the Lord" (Hab 3:18); "exult in your name all the day" (Psa 89:16); "to God my exceeding joy" (Psa 43:4). The human-to-God direction is the primary mode of this characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes — this is the dominant direction in M04-B-VCG-05 (90 verses of God-directed psalmist and prophetic gladness) and throughout M04-C. The human-to-God direction includes: direct "rejoice in the Lord" commands (Psa 32:11; 97:12; Phili 4:4; 3:1); rejoicing in God's salvation as the psalmist's oriented movement (Psa 9:2; 14:7; 35:9; 53:6; 63:11; Isa 25:9; 61:10); the feast-joy before God at his sanctuary (Deu 12:7, 18; 16:11–15 — the spatial movement of Israel to the chosen place and the inner movement toward God); praise, thanksgiving, and prayer accompanying joy (Psa 100:2; Jer 33:11; Phili 4:4–6).

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: (1) **Worship and prayer** — Luk 10:21 (Jesus' agalliao immediately moves into addressed prayer: "I thank you, Father") — Suffering-Joy is the inner state that generates worshipful movement toward the Father; Luk 1:47 (Mary's spirit exults "in God my Savior" — the exultation is directed toward God as its object); Act 2:26 (tongue rejoicing → "my flesh also will dwell in hope" — the movement toward trust in God); (2) **Continued faithful mission** — Act 5:41 (apostles' rejoicing → continued teaching — the movement toward God through faithful mission-action); (3) **Joyful endurance** — Heb 12:2 (Christ's joy-grounded endurance of the cross — the cross as the climactic movement toward the Father's purpose).

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. (1) **Doxological movement** — the ki-tov praise declarations (Psa 100:5; 106:1 — "give thanks to the Lord, for he is good") are the human person's movement toward God in recognition of his goodness; the formula frames thanksgiving and praise as the inner movement prompted by Gladness-recognition; (2) **Seeking** — Lam 3:25–26 ("the Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him") — seeking God is the human movement that positions the person to experience his goodness; (3) **Gratitude** — Ezr 3:11 ("for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever toward Israel" — responsive praise at the temple foundation); Deu 8:10 ("you shall bless the Lord your God for the good land") — receiving the good land occasions the movement of blessing toward God; (4) **Trust** — the entire M04-O-VCG-04 register shows the human person trusting in God's good promises as a movement of the inner being toward him.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, in M04-G and M04-H's upward registers: (1) **Affective upward movement** — Psa 37:4 ("delight yourself in the Lord") — commanded upward orientation of the inner being toward God as its object; Isa 58:14 ("you shall take delight in the Lord") — Delight as the human person's movement toward God; Job 22:26 (future delight in the Almighty); Job 27:10 (the hypocrite who will not delight in the Almighty — exposing the expected upward movement as absent); (2) **Delight in God's word as movement toward God** — Psa 119 series (delight in statutes, testimonies, commandments, law — all as God's self-expression); Rom 7:22 ("I delight in the law of God, in my inner being") — the innermost self moving toward God through his word; (3) **Obedience-Delight** (M04-M) — Joh 8:29; 1Jo 3:22 — the soul's movement toward what pleases God as the sustaining orientation of the inner person's upward relationship; (4) **Seeking God's presence as Delight** — Psa 73:28 ("it is good to be near God") — the human person's inner experience of divine nearness as the supreme good, motivating continued movement toward it; (5) **Neh 1:11** — "who delight to fear your name" — the soul's reverential Delight in God's name as the form of upward movement.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes: (1) **Psa 27:4** — "one thing have I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord… to gaze upon the beauty of the Lord" — the entire movement of the seeking person toward God is motivated by and culminates in Pleasure (gazing upon divine beauty); (2) **The ni.cho.ach worship acts** (M04-K-VCG-01) — the worshiper's act of offering correctly-prepared sacrifice is a movement toward God that produces the pleasing-aroma Pleasure relationship; human-to-God Pleasure operates through worship action; (3) **Psa 147:1** — "for it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant and a song of praise is fitting" — the pleasantness of praise as the experience of human worship-movement toward God; (4) **Psa 135:3** — "praise the Lord… for it is pleasant!" — pleasantness of worship as the felt quality of the human movement toward God in praise.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **Wonder producing worship-movement** — the proclamatory corpus is consistently doxological: "sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wondrous works" (1Ch 16:9) — Wonder moves the person toward God in praise; "I will give thanks to the Lord with my whole heart; I will recount all of your wonderful deeds" (Psa 9:1) — Wonder producing wholehearted Godward movement; (2) **Seeking to behold** — Psa 119:18 ("open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law") — Wonder-seeking in the law as movement toward God through his word; (3) **Contemplative movement** — Psa 119:27 ("make me understand the way of your precepts, and I will meditate on your wondrous works"); Psa 145:5 ("on your wondrous works, I will meditate") — sustained contemplative movement toward God through Wonder-meditation; (4) **Job's return** — Job 42:3 ("things too wonderful for me, which I did not know") — Job's Wonder-humility as the restored posture of a person returned to right relationship with God.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven evidence human-to-God operation, but with different relational profiles: (1) **Most dominantly human-to-God**: Exultation (Char 1) — the entire VCG-01 corpus is human exultation directed toward God (Psa 35:9; Isa 61:10; Hab 3:18); (2) **Extensively human-to-God**: Joy (Char 2) — M04-B-VCG-05 (90 verses of God-directed psalmist joy) and M04-C throughout; Wonder (Char 6) — the proclamatory corpus is consistently Godward (Psa 9:1; 1Ch 16:9); (3) **Devotionally human-to-God**: Delight (Char 4) — Psa 37:4 (delight yourself in the Lord), Psa 73:25 (nothing on earth I desire besides you), M04-G throughout; Gladness (Char 3) — ki-tov praise as Godward gladness-declaration; (4) **Worship-mediated human-to-God**: Pleasure (Char 5) — Psa 27:4 (seeking to gaze on God's beauty), ni.cho.ach worship-offering as human-to-God Pleasure-act; (5) **Paradox-grounded human-to-God**: Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — Luk 10:21 (Jesus' Spirit-rejoicing moving immediately into prayer to the Father); Luk 1:47 (Mary's spirit exulting in God my Savior). The cluster is primarily Godward: the seven characteristics are most fully realised when directed toward God as their object. Psa 43:4's "God my exceeding joy" names the characteristic's ultimate Godward orientation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, and the M07-C corpus (M07-C-VCG-01 and -03) is the primary evidence. The person in the M07-C mode moves toward God *through* shame: the penitential posture of lying down in shame (Jer 3:25, vc=37308/37470), the inability to lift the face to God that nonetheless constitutes a kind of prayer (Ezr 9:6), the conscience-driven shame that moves toward renewed service (2Ch 30:15). The M07-C-VCG-02 material shows the complementary movement: the person's movement toward God through trust simultaneously protects from shame — these are the two faces of the human-toward-God movement in shame's register (moving toward God through shame's guilt; moving toward God through trust and word). Both are movements toward God; they differ in what drives them (guilt-shame vs. confident trust).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Limited evidence. Eze 44:13 — Levites bearing shame as a restriction on their approach to God — shows CHAR-2 governing human-to-God access in the priestly context. CHAR-2 does not primarily operate as a human movement toward God; it is imposed on humans from God or from other humans.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Extensively evidenced in VCG-01. Joh 8:49 — "you dishonor me" (Jesus = God incarnate); Rom 2:23 — "you dishonor God by breaking the law"; Heb 6:6 — apostates "hold him up to contempt." The human-to-God direction of CHAR-3 is the active worth-denial of God's incarnate person and his moral authority. The inner posture required to avoid CHAR-3 toward God is described in its absence in Luk 18:2 — fearing God is the inner posture that prevents CHAR-3 toward God.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — The idolatrous-shameful-objects register (VCG-01 — Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) is precisely about what the human conscience should assess as shameful in relation to God: the idol is "the shameful thing" (bo.shet — Jer 3:24) that has replaced God in the person's movement toward him. CHAR-4's proper functioning toward God means assessing idolatrous objects as shameful and recoiling from them toward God.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Human-to-God CHAR-5 is evidenced in the mockery of Jesus (Luk 23:11 — Herod and his soldiers treating Jesus with contempt and mockery). The acts directed at Jesus in his passion are CHAR-5 in its most concentrated form: the world's contempt-verdict on God incarnate. Act 4:11 (the builders rejecting the cornerstone) shows the human rejection of God's sent-one as CHAR-5 directed toward God through the mediating agency of Jesus. The inner posture that prevents CHAR-5 toward God is the recognition of divine worth — receiving the despised as "an angel of God, as Christ Jesus" (Gal 4:14).

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The primary human-to-God direction of CHAR-6 is worship and approach: Psa 26:6 — "I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, O Lord" — is the movement of the innocent person toward God in the cultic act of going around the altar. CHAR-6 is what enables this movement. The inner posture required is moral cleanness — the person who approaches God must have their inner moral condition aligned with the holiness they approach.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human-to-God movement across M07 concentrates in three registers. (1) Shame-mediated approach — the guilt-shame of Char 1 (M07-C) and the innocence-enabled approach of Char 6 constitute the two poles of the human-to-God encounter: shame as recognition of moral inadequacy before holiness (Ezr 9:6); innocence as the condition enabling approach without guilt's barrier (Psa 26:6). These two poles are the cluster's most theologically significant human-to-God dimension. (2) Dishonour and contempt directed at God incarnate — Chars 3 and 5 evidence the human actively dishonouring God incarnate (Joh 8:49; Rom 2:23) and directing contempt toward Jesus (Luk 23:11). These are the most theologically acute forms of CHAR-3 and CHAR-5. (3) Shamefulness as covenant infidelity — Char 4's idolatrous-shameful-objects register (Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) shows the human movement toward God corrupted when idolatry produces the shameful object that displaces God.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes — as the inner state that blocks every form of human-to-God movement. Psa 10:4 (vc=34074, M08-A2-VCG-02): "the wicked does not seek him; all his thoughts are, 'there is no God'" — CHAR-1 displaces the act of seeking God entirely, substituting self-sufficient cognitive closure for the movement of seeking. Hos 7:10 (vc=34001, M08-A3-VCG-03): "the pride of Israel testifies to his face; yet they do not return to the Lord their God, nor seek him, for all this" — the movement of return (repentance, covenant re-engagement) is specifically blocked by CHAR-1. Isa 26:10 (vc=34024, M08-A4-VCG-05): "the wicked person's inner perceptual faculty is closed to the Lord's majesty even in a land of uprightness" — even environmental conditions that should prompt God-ward movement (righteousness all around) are insufficient to overcome CHAR-1's blockage. Deu 8:14 (vc=34223, M08-A1-VCG-01): the heart lifted up forgets God — forgetfulness replaces the memory of God's redemptive acts that would motivate worship and gratitude.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes — as the characteristic that directly opposes the human person's movement toward God. Psa 86:14 (vc=34097, M08-B-VCG-02): "they do not set God before them" — CHAR-2 removes God from the directional horizon of the inner person's movement. Neh 9:16 (vc=34120, M08-B-VCG-01): "they did not obey your commandments" — the obedience that is the vehicle of human-to-God movement is specifically what CHAR-2 refuses. Jer 50:29 (vc=34127, M08-B-VCG-01): "she has defied the Lord, the Holy One of Israel" — CHAR-2 directed explicitly against the divine person, inverting the movement of human-to-God approach into direct opposition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes — in two opposite modes. VCG-01 negative: Rom 2:17 (vc=33882, M08-C-VCG-01): "you who call yourself a Jew and rely on the law and boast in God" — the person using religious identity as the ground of self-boasting; the boast is directed "in God" but is actually a self-promotion using religious credentials, not genuine God-directed movement. VCG-03 positive: Phili 3:3 (vc=33879, M08-C-VCG-03): "worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh" — the VCG-03 glorying is genuine movement toward God; Rom 5:11 (vc=33876, M08-C-VCG-03): "we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ."

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — as the characteristic that distorts the cognitive self-assessment foundational to accurate movement toward God. The inner act of intercession is the human-to-God movement that corresponds to the God-to-human act of forgiving.
- Group 5379-002 description: "the act of seeking God's pardon on behalf of oneself or others, and God's response of pardoning or withholding." The seeking-act is the human movement; the pardoning is the divine response.

**Access-postures as human-to-God orientations:**
- Repentance (Mar 1:4; Act 2:38): the inner turning of the person toward God — a directional movement from self-toward-sin to self-toward-God.
- Faith (Act 10:43): the inner orientation of trust toward God as the one who forgives through Christ.
- Confession (1Jo 1:9): the verbal inner act directed toward God — the acknowledgement of sin spoken toward the one who can resolve it.
- Prayer (Mar 11:25): "whenever you stand praying, forgive" — the forgiveness act is embedded in the posture of prayer, which is itself a human-to-God orientation.

Zec 12:10 (anchor): pleas for mercy poured out by the spirit of grace. The human-to-God direction of grace is the supplication posture — the creature's appeal for what it cannot supply.

Yes — the human-to-God direction is well-evidenced through the supplication vocabulary, which is structurally embedded in the compassion data as a significant XREF set.

**Supplication as the human-to-God compassion-interface:** H8467 techinah (supplication, 24 XREF occurrences) and H8469 tahanun (entreaty, 18 XREF occurrences) both derive from the CHANAN root (grace/favour/compassion). They name the verbal acts through which the human person appeals for divine compassion. The structural relationship established by this vocabulary: God's compassion is the presupposed ground that makes earnest appeal possible (SD-021). The human person who approaches God in supplication is acting on the knowledge that God is compassionate — the appeal would be irrational if God were not.

**Psalm vocabulary of seeking chesed:** Psa 25:7 (group 1633-003) — "according to your steadfast love remember me" — is directed toward God. Psa 48:9 — "we have thought on your steadfast love, O God, in the midst of your temple." These are human-to-God movements in which the human inner being orients itself toward and rests in divine chesed. This is not supplication under duress but contemplative orientation — the human person's inner being actively seeking and dwelling in the reality of divine compassion.

**Covenantal return enabled by compassion (Joel 2:13):** "Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and merciful (rachum ve-channum)." The divine compassion-character is the basis and motivation for the human movement back toward God. The human-to-God direction here is one of return — the inner act of repentance and reorientation toward God, enabled and motivated by the certainty of his compassion.

Yes — contrition is constitutively a movement of the human toward God. All five Dependence/Creatureliness groups describe a human inner being in posture *before God* — the orientation is upward and toward God. The contrite person brings their broken spirit and heart to God (Psa 51:17 — offered as sacrifice), appeals to God from their crushed position (Psa 51:8; Psa 143:3), and trembles before God's word (Isa 66:2). The human-to-God movement is the constitutive direction of contrition in its penitential-relational mode.

Yes. The human-to-God direction is the second best-evidenced direction.

**Pursuit-fellowship:** Phili 3:10 — *that I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share his sufferings* — Paul's statement is an expression of active seeking-fellowship with God: the movement is entirely from Paul toward Christ. This is the clearest human-to-God fellowship act in the evidence.

**Companionship as God-oriented:** Psa 119:63 — *I am a companion of all who fear you, of those who keep your precepts* — the human person's orientation toward God (fear of God, precept-keeping) grounds the human-to-God relational movement. This is fellowship with God expressed through fellowship with God's community.

**Group 873-001 description** — the vertical fellowship involves participation in divine nature, the Son, and the Spirit — which necessarily involves human movement toward God, not only God's movement toward the human.

Human-to-God operation is evidenced through three modes: (1) Doxological worship — the liturgical refrain "for he is good, his steadfast love endures forever" (group 884-001) is goodness operating as the content of the human's praise and confession toward God. The human declares God's goodness in worship — this is goodness moving upward from the human toward God as acknowledgement and adoration. (2) Seeking and trust — Psa 34:8 ("blessed is the man who takes refuge in him") and Lam 3:25 ("the soul who seeks him"): the human's movement toward God in trust and seeking is enabled by the encounter with divine goodness. Goodness produces the movement toward God. (3) Covenantal request — Psa 119:68 ("you are good and do good; teach me your statutes"): the human addresses God's goodness as the ground for petition. God's goodness is invoked as the basis of the human's request — "because you are good, teach me." (OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-026, OBS-067-OBS-033)

Human love toward God is the great commandment's content: love with all heart, soul, and mind (Mat 22:37, OBS-103-139). The data shows love toward God expressed through: (a) **Total mobilisation** — 'with all your heart and soul and mind' — no faculty withheld; (b) **Commandment-keeping** — 'if you love me, you will keep my commandments' (Joh 14:15, OBS-103-140) — love produces the obedience-pattern; (c) **Priority-ranking** — love of God above family love (Mat 10:37, OBS-103-151), above love of the present world (2Ti 4:10, OBS-103-148); (d) **Costly following** — Jer 2:2 (OBS-103-098) — Israel's early love expressed through following God into the wilderness; (e) **Praise** — Psa 63:3 (OBS-103-087): 'because your steadfast love is better than life, my lips will praise you' — love toward God expressed as praise. The human-to-God direction is constituted by total inner mobilisation, life-ordering, and expressive acts.

Yes — the human-toward-God direction is extensively evidenced as the responsive axis of the covenant relationship. (1) Covenant entry as movement toward God: Neh 10:29 — "enter into a curse and an oath to walk in God's Law" — the community moves toward God through formal covenantal commitment (OBS-034-035). 2Ki 23:3 — the king "made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord" — covenant-making is explicitly a movement toward God (OBS-034-047). (2) Covenant-keeping as sustained movement: Deu 7:9 — "those who love him and keep his commandments" — sustained love and commandment-keeping as the ongoing human posture toward God within the covenant (OBS-034-039). Psa 25:10 — "those who keep his covenant and his testimonies" — covenant-keeping as a description of the person who walks with God. (3) Confession of covenant breach as movement back toward God: Dan 9:11 (OBS-034-036) — Daniel's prayer is a movement of confessional return toward God after covenant failure — using covenantal language to re-engage the God whose covenant has been broken. (4) Swearing by God's name as allegiance (3308-003 — OBS-034-055): taking an oath in God's name as an act of inner allegiance directed toward God.

Yes — several forms. (1) Making peace with God: Isa 27:5 ("let them make peace with me, let them make peace with me") — the human act of coming into covenant relationship with God; (2) Walking with God in peace: Mal 2:6 — the sustained human posture of covenant faithfulness expressed as peace-with-God; (3) Returning to God: Isa 30:15 ("in returning and rest you shall be saved") — returning to God as the peace-generating human act (even though the peace itself is God's gift, the returning is the human movement toward God); (4) Praying for peace: Psa 122:6 ("pray for the peace of Jerusalem") — intercession as the human peace-orientation toward God on behalf of community; (5) The soul waiting in silence (Psa 62:5 — 2585-001) — "for God alone, O my soul, wait in silence" — the posture of the soul directed toward God in peaceful expectation.

Yes — group 872-005 and 872-006 together evidence the human-to-God direction. (1) Glory-giving (872-006): Jer 13:16 (OBS-060-047) — humans commanded to give glory to God. This is a directed movement of the human inner person toward God: the act of ascribing worth, acknowledging God's reality, orienting the inner life Godward. (2) Worship (872-005): Gen 12:7 — Abram builds an altar immediately after receiving the covenantal promise. This worship-response is the human giving of self in gratitude and recognition.
